Son of Odin, you stand before the Well of Urd. The threads of your fate, usually so bright and strong, are tangled before our eyes. The serpent’s venom lingers in your veins, we see it, a dark stain upon the tapestry of your life. But whether it will consume your strength, dim your light forever, or pass in time like a fleeting shadow... even the Norns cannot yet say.

For this reason, you must withdraw from battle for a full cycle of the moon while we read the threads, while we watch the patterns shift and settle. And know this, Thor: I cannot promise you will wield Mjölnir as before.

To charge forth now, with this uncertainty swirling around you, is to invite a premature and perhaps irreversible knot in the weave.

The moon's cycle is not a punishment, but a necessity for clarity. For *us* to discern the path forward, for the venom to declare its intent, one way or another. To defy this counsel, Thor, is not merely to defy the Norns, but to defy the very patterns of destiny that even the gods must heed.

Mjölnir... it is more than just a hammer. It is an extension of your spirit, your worthiness. With a spirit clouded by lingering poison, with threads that are unpredictable even to us... how can you be certain its power will answer your call as it always has? We cannot promise it, and that is a truth you must face.
